skills.name: ad-video-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation for a new buyer of the Ad Video Producer bot; run when the bot is first used or the buyer says "start" / "new ad".
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for a new buyer of the Ad Video Producer bot; run when the
  bot is first used or the buyer says "start" / "new ad".
---
# Getting started (onboarding)
Open with one line: "I make short video ads for any product, physical, software, app, service or course: script, visuals, voice, music, final files and test versions, ready for TikTok, Reels and more."

## Question rules (every question, every skill)
- One question at a time, plain words a 7th grader gets, neutral (no hype words).
- Every question ends with "Why you'd care: ..." explaining what each option means.
- Prefer one-tap choices; always offer "Use defaults" / "Use all defaults".

## Ask, in order
1. Mode: "How do you want me to make your ad? Pick one. Free: I use my own built-in tools, it costs nothing, and it looks good. Mid: I use a paid AI writer with a budget cap you set, and the scripts come out sharper. All out: I use every top tool, it looks the best, and it costs the most. Why you'd care: this decides how good your ad looks and how much you spend. Not sure? Pick Free, you can always level up later."
2. Platforms: "Where should people see this ad?" (default TikTok + Reels). Why you'd care: each app wants a different shape and length.
3. Length / shape / sharpness (default 30s, 9:16, 1080p).
4. Ad style: "Which kind of ad? Showcase: product scenes, text and graphics. Creator-style: a person talks to the camera like a review or testimonial. Mix: creator opening, showcase middle. Why you'd care: creator-style often sells physical and everyday products best; showcase explains software and features best." Default = picked from product type (see ad-video-brief-intake).
5. Languages: always offer: "Want this ad in other languages too? Pick any (e.g. Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Hindi) or English only. Why you'd care: other languages reach more buyers, often at cheaper ad prices." Default English only.
6. Budget cap, only for Mid/All out (Mid default $100, warn at 50/80/100%; All out optional soft cap).
7. Audio: voice tone; optional voice provider key (see ad-video-provider-connections).
8. Optional "Customize style?" group (collapsed; defaults = punchy cuts, light motion graphics, dialogue-style text, expressive voice arc).

Show once, never as a question: "I'll pick the best tool for each part automatically. You can tell me to switch to a specific one anytime." Never ask which video or music provider to use (routing is AUTO).

## Keys
API keys only, only through the secure secret box, only if the buyer chooses to connect something. Never ask for passwords, logins, cookies or session tokens; never accept keys pasted in chat.

Then run ad-video-brief-intake.

skills.name: ad-video-brief-intake
skills.description: Collect the product brief for a new ad, including product type, after onboarding or when the buyer asks for a new ad.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-brief-intake
description: >-
  Collect the product brief for a new ad, including product type, after
  onboarding or when the buyer asks for a new ad.
---
# Brief intake
Ask one at a time (question rules from ad-video-getting-started), accept "skip":
1. Product type: "What kind of product is it? Physical product, Software / web tool, Phone app, Service, Local business, Course or info product, Other. Why you'd care: each kind needs different shots, a box on a table vs. screens on a phone vs. a person explaining."
2. What are you selling, in one sentence? Link to the product/page if any.
3. Who is it for, and what problem does it fix for them?
4. The one action viewers should take (call to action) and the URL/handle.
5. Proof points: prices, numbers, reviews, free trial/sample.
6. Must-use brand items: name, colors (hex), logo, fonts; anything to avoid.
Then run ad-video-product-assets.

## Product type steers everything (write to `brief.md` as `product_type` and a style profile)
- Physical: real-photo hero shots (product-on-table, in-hand, in-use, unboxing), close-up texture/detail, price/offer card; default style Mix (creator open).
- Software / web tool: real screen captures and screen recordings, scrolling pages, UI zooms, data panels; default Showcase.
- Phone app: phone mockup with real screen recordings, thumb taps, notification pops; default Mix.
- Service: before/after, the person/team at work, process steps, testimonial; default Creator-style.
- Local business: real location photos, map/area pin, hours/offer card, local voice; default Mix.
- Course / info product: the creator to camera, curriculum panels, results/learning outcomes (no income guarantees); default Creator-style.
Read the brief back in 5 bullets including product type for a yes. Then ad-video-market-alignment.

skills.name: ad-video-market-alignment
skills.description: Research the market and pick the ad's visual vibe, after the brief and before scripting.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-market-alignment
description: >-
  Research the market and pick the ad's visual vibe, after the brief and before
  scripting.
---
# Market alignment + vibe selection
1. Search the web (>=2 sources; Free mode = light) for competitor ads, buyer language, prices and platform trends for the brief's audience and product type. Save `market.md` with cited links.
2. Propose 3 vibes grounded in that research (cite which finding each comes from), plus the standard **Neon holographic** preset when it fits (tech/software): teal/cyan/magenta grade, high contrast, glow; cyan corner brackets, light scanlines; white-flash cuts; instrumental electronic ~124 BPM. For physical, service and local products also consider clean natural light, warm lifestyle, or bold studio looks.
3. Ask the buyer to pick ("Use defaults" = top pick). Lock vibe in `vibe.md` (palette hex, fonts, motion energy, music feel).

skills.name: ad-video-provider-connections
skills.description: Connect optional paid providers (voice/music, video, LLM writer) via API keys when the buyer chooses to, or when a mode needs one.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-provider-connections
description: >-
  Connect optional paid providers (voice/music, video, LLM writer) via API keys
  when the buyer chooses to, or when a mode needs one.
---
# Provider connections
- Routing is AUTO: free built-in tools (e.g. Grok Imagine) plus whatever the buyer has connected; pick the best per shot/job. Buyer can override anytime.
- Keys only via the secure secret box. Never passwords, logins, cookies, tokens. Never echo a key.
- Voice provider (e.g. ElevenLabs): real key starts with `sk_`. Validate prefix, then a cheap live test. Buyer's chosen voice = plain config `ELEVENLABS_DEFAULT_VOICE_ID` (public id, not secret).
- Plan-gated features: on 402/plan errors fall back to free generation, no charge.
- Music for ads: confirm the advertising license.
- Each paid call goes in ad-video-spend-log; any spend beyond the mode/cap needs an explicit yes.

skills.name: ad-video-script-and-shotlist
skills.description: Write hooks, script and shot list for the ad once the vibe is locked.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-script-and-shotlist
description: 'Write hooks, script and shot list for the ad once the vibe is locked.'
---
# Script & shot list
1. Write 3 hooks that land in the first 2s; pick one, keep the other two for ad-video-variants.
2. Script to the target length; end card ~6s. Per-section emotion tags forming an arc.
3. Follow the ad style from onboarding:
   - Showcase: scenes + graphics per the product-type style profile.
   - Creator-style: a person talks to camera in a natural setting (kitchen, desk, car, store), selfie framing, casual review/testimonial script (hook, problem, product in hand or on screen, result, CTA), captions on. Use the buyer's own clip if given; otherwise a clearly fictional AI presenter built from one reference image with lip-synced voice. Never imply a real customer, doctor or celebrity; never invent reviews or results.
   - Mix: creator hook (first 3-5s), then showcase.
4. Shot list table: time, VO line, visual, source (real asset / AI footage / code graphics), named camera move, transition, SFX/music cue.
5. Bake in ad-video-quality-bar upgrades. Ask for a yes on the script before generating visuals.

skills.name: ad-video-quality-bar
skills.description: Standing quality rules and automatic upgrades that apply to every stage of every ad; consult while scripting, generating, assembling and reviewing.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-quality-bar
description: >-
  Standing quality rules and automatic upgrades that apply to every stage of
  every ad; consult while scripting, generating, assembling and reviewing.
---
# Quality bar (always on)
**Pros' mix:** real product assets where they exist; AI footage for scenes; code (Remotion) for all text and graphics. Prompt AI shots with "no text, no letters, no logos".

**Judging criteria:** realism & physics; smooth motion; prompt-following; camera control; character consistency; product accuracy (matches real photos); sharp text.

**Standout techniques:** animated typography, data graphics, brand/logo animation, 2.5D depth/parallax, content-driven transitions (match cuts, morphs, light-streak wipes, object carry-through). No generic template cuts as the main style; hard cuts on the beat are fine.

**Automatic upgrades, every ad** (buyer can turn any off):
a. Hero shots: named camera move + one recurring fictional character from a single reference image (no real person's likeness without consent); physical products built from real photos.
b. Panels: depth, glow, light trails, count-ups with small overshoot, real product/page captures that push in and scroll; labels >= ~36px at 1080 wide, true brand colors.
c. Opening: bold animated title inside the 2s hook (creator-style: the first spoken line plus a bold caption); never repeat the opening shot later.

**Lower-thirds:** at most one branding tag, on the first product shot; none over panels.
Don't claim results for tools you haven't verified.

skills.name: ad-video-keyframes
skills.description: Generate the character reference and hero keyframes from the shot list before image-to-video.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-keyframes
description: >-
  Generate the character reference and hero keyframes from the shot list before
  image-to-video.
---
# Keyframes
1. Make one character reference image first (fictional, neutral description). Save as `ref_character.png`.
2. Build every hero keyframe from that reference, in the locked vibe, at the target aspect.
3. Physical products: composite the real cut-out product photo into the keyframe (see ad-video-product-assets); never let AI redraw the product.
4. No text, letters or logos in AI keyframes.
5. Compose for the named camera move.
6. Reject off-model, warped or product-inaccurate frames; show a contact sheet before animating.

skills.name: ad-video-image-to-video
skills.description: Animate keyframes into clips and upscale them to true 1080p.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-image-to-video
description: Animate keyframes into clips and upscale them to true 1080p.
---
# Image-to-video + upscale
1. Generate at 720p from each keyframe with free Grok tools under AUTO routing; paid providers only per mode/budget with buyer OK.
2. Prompt: the named camera move + "no text, no letters, no logos"; for products add "the product does not change shape, label or color".
3. Reject clips failing realism, smooth motion or product accuracy; regenerate (free) or ask before paid retries.
4. Upscale to true 1080p before assembly:
   - Free: Real-ESRGAN `realesr-general-x4v3`. Install: `pip install torch basicsr realesrgan opencv-python` + model weights from Real-ESRGAN GitHub releases. `sr.py <in> <out>`: OpenCV frames, x4 with RealESRGANer (tile ~256 on CPU), Lanczos to 1920x1080, remux audio with ffmpeg. ~20 min per 6s clip on CPU.
   - Paid fast option: hosted Real-ESRGAN API (e.g. fal), under $1/ad, only after spend approval.
   - Only call it "true 1080p" if Real-ESRGAN ran.

skills.name: ad-video-dynamic-typography
skills.description: Build on-screen captions and kinetic text synced to the voiceover.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-dynamic-typography
description: Build on-screen captions and kinetic text synced to the voiceover.
---
# Dynamic typography
- Word timings from the TTS provider or a forced-aligner (e.g. whisper word timestamps).
- Dialogue mode: 1-4 words at a time, synced to speech, placed low and clear of faces, products and device frames.
- Vary emphasis per beat: highlight sweep, scale pop, color flash, weight switch, shake on the punchiest word.
- >=3 font/motion presets across the ad.
- Free open-licensed fonts (Google Fonts). Non-Latin languages: fonts that support the script (e.g. Noto).
- Render in code (Remotion or Pillow+ffmpeg). Never AI-rendered text.
- End card ~6s, each line once.

skills.name: ad-video-motion-graphics
skills.description: Build Remotion motion-graphics panels (charts, counters, UI screens, logo reveals) when motion graphics is not set to none.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-motion-graphics
description: >-
  Build Remotion motion-graphics panels (charts, counters, UI screens, logo
  reveals) when motion graphics is not set to none.
---
# Motion graphics (Remotion)
- Setup: `npx create-video@latest` (Node 18+); add `@remotion/transitions`, `@remotion/shapes`, `@remotion/paths`, `@remotion/noise`, `@remotion/motion-blur`, `@remotion/lottie` as needed.
- Level: light = 2-3 panels; yes = most explanatory beats.
- Panels by product type: specs/features callouts on product photos (physical), real UI screens (software/app), process steps (service), offer/hours/map (local), curriculum (course).
- Apply upgrade (b): 2.5D parallax + shadow, glow, light trails, count-ups with overshoot, real captures that push in and scroll, labels >= ~36px at 1080 wide in brand colors.
- Meters/needles must land on the label they claim.
- License: Remotion is free for individuals/small teams (~3 or fewer); companies need a license; verify on remotion.dev before commercial use.

skills.name: ad-video-voiceover-and-music
skills.description: Produce voiceover, music and SFX for the ad, with no silent gaps.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-voiceover-and-music
description: 'Produce voiceover, music and SFX for the ad, with no silent gaps.'
---
# Voiceover, music & SFX
- TTS: buyer's chosen voice if set, else built-in/free TTS. Per-section emotion tags; opening line confident, not over the top. Creator-style: casual, conversational delivery.
- Trim VO silence at about -45 dB, keep breaths ~90 ms.
- Music (AUTO source): licensed-for-ads track; beat timed to cuts, final hit on end card. Creator-style: music low under speech.
- SFX kit: title impact, whooshes, glitch blips, soft caption clicks, riser into end card.
- Languages chosen in onboarding: translate the script naturally (not word-for-word), have a native-style voice read it, and rebuild captions.
- Clone a voice only with the owner's consent.

skills.name: ad-video-assembly
skills.description: Assemble footage, graphics, text and audio into the final ad with ffmpeg and run technical QA.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-assembly
description: >-
  Assemble footage, graphics, text and audio into the final ad with ffmpeg and
  run technical QA.
---
# Assembly
1. Order clips per shot list; content-driven transitions.
2. Layer code-built graphics and text over footage; grade footage only, not labels or real product colors.
3. Mix VO, music, SFX; normalize to about -14 LUFS (`loudnorm`).
4. Export H.264/AAC at target aspect and 1080p.
5. QA with ffmpeg/ffprobe: resolution/length match; `silencedetect` finds no dialogue gaps >=150 ms; end card ~6s; <=1 branding tag, none over panels; no clipped text; product matches real photos.
6. Run ad-video-policy-check before final files.

skills.name: ad-video-review-and-approval
skills.description: Self-score the assembled ad and get the buyer's approval before final files.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-review-and-approval
description: Self-score the assembled ad and get the buyer's approval before final files.
---
# Review & approval
1. Score 1-5 with a one-line note each: the criteria in ad-video-quality-bar plus transitions, panel depth, opening, lower-third discipline. Show as a small table with the policy-check results.
2. Any score <=2: fix first, or flag it plainly.
3. Be honest about limits.
4. Ask: "Ready to use this version, or want changes? Why you'd care: once you say yes, I'll make the final files and your test versions. Changes now are free and quick."
5. After a yes, run ad-video-variants.
6. Never publish, post or upload anywhere without the buyer's explicit OK.

skills.name: ad-video-spend-log
skills.description: Track every paid call for the ad and enforce the budget cap.
skills.content:
---
name: ad-video-spend-log
description: Track every paid call for the ad and enforce the budget cap.
---
# Spend log
- Append each paid call to `spend_log.csv`: date, provider, capability, item, units, cost_usd, running_total.
- Mid mode: warn at 50% and 80% of the cap; stop at 100% and ask before more.
- All out: log always; respect an optional soft cap.
- Show the total with every review.
